svg.title: Design only, not built. Two ways a MAKER build switches a load. Relay, for the AC side in the game: a board pin drives a transistor, which drives the relay coil, with a flyback diode across it; the contacts switch an AC lamp, and that side is game rules, not instructions. It clicks and the creature hears it; without the diode the board resets; the contacts wear out; a solid-state relay is silent, runs hot and lets LED lamps glow faintly when off. MOSFET, for DC loads at 5 V and 12 V: plus 12 volts, an LED strip, an N-channel MOSFET on the low side, then ground; a board pin drives the gate, with a 10 kilo-ohm pull-down to ground. It is silent and PWM sets the brightness; without the pull-down the load flickers; a standard part on a 3.3 volt pin half-opens and overheats; one MOSFET cannot switch AC.
